**Real file and folder dates.** In v0.1.0 everything in a drive showed as
1 Jan 1601 on Windows and 1 Jan 1970 on macOS. Now each file and folder shows
its actual modified, created and accessed dates.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.1.1-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `cloak-v0.1.1-macos-universal.zip` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

Each zip has `cloak` (CLI), `cloak-gui` (desktop app) and the mount adapter
(`cloak-winmount.exe` on Windows, `cloak-mount` on macOS). Keep them in the
same folder: the app launches the adapter from next to itself.

The binaries are not code-signed. On macOS, clear the download quarantine
before first run: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine cloak-v0.1.1-macos-universal`.

## What's new

- **Dates are shown.** Each item takes the dates of its disguised file in the
  store folder. Those were already visible to anyone looking at that folder,
  so nothing new is revealed. Existing drives work as they are: no
  conversion, they just start showing real dates.
- **Dates are kept.** Copying files in with Explorer, Directory Opus,
  `robocopy /COPY:DAT`, `cp -p` or Finder keeps their original dates, and
  `touch` works.
- **Backups and sync behave.** Tools that compare dates (`robocopy /MIR`,
  rsync, sync apps) no longer see every file as changed on every run.

## Known limitations

- **The macOS mount has still not been tested on a real Mac.** It builds and
  the shared engine is fully tested, but treat it as a preview and keep a
  backup of anything you put in a drive.
- Renaming something inside a folder doesn't update that folder's modified
  date (creating or deleting something in it does).
- FUSE-T is not supported yet (macFUSE only).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
